en.title: FishBase
en.summary: Global finfish biodiversity database covering taxonomy, biology, ecology, life history, distributions, fisheries uses, images, references, and collaborator provenance.
en.description: FishBase is a global biodiversity information system for finfishes. It began as a population-dynamics reference for 200 major commercial species and now covers all known fish species across taxonomy, nomenclature, biology, trophic ecology, life history, morphology, distribution, fisheries uses, conservation and vulnerability context, common names, images, and literature provenance. The live website reports more than 36,500 species, more than 333,000 common names, more than 65,800 pictures, more than 68,300 references, more than 2,570 collaborators, more than 700,000 monthly visits, and approximately 3.3 million records across about 200 tables. FishBase is hosted and managed by Quantitative Aquatics, Inc. (Q-quatics), with scientific guidance from a 13-member FishBase Consortium. Researchers usually access FishBase through the free web UI and species summaries; technical users can query static backend snapshots as CSV/parquet through Source Cooperative and the rfishbase R package. Contributions are curated rather than directly written to the core database: contributors can submit observations, photos, reprints, corrections, or datasets through FishBase collaborator and FishWatcher workflows. The public parquet snapshot is compressed, versioned, and may lag the live website.

en.title: SeaLifeBase
en.summary: Global aquatic biodiversity database for non-fish aquatic organisms, with taxonomy, traits, distribution, ecology, images, references, and public table snapshots.
en.description: SeaLifeBase is a global biodiversity information system for marine and freshwater organisms other than finfishes. It extends the FishBase-style record model to invertebrates, algae, marine mammals, reptiles, birds, and other aquatic taxa, covering taxonomy, synonyms, common names, life-history traits, ecology, country and ecosystem distributions, AquaMaps-linked map data, images, references, and collaborator provenance. The public v25.04 search-statistics snapshot reports 71,911 species records, 60,126 common names, 15,737 pictures, 40,479 references, 143,101 synonyms, 371 collaborators, and 500,000 sessions. Q-quatics maintains the FishBase/SeaLifeBase technical family, with Sea Around Us and the broader FishBase/SeaLifeBase community providing scientific context. Human web access is through SeaLifeBase mirror sites and species-summary pages, but those mirrors can present Cloudflare verification to automated clients; technical users should prefer the versioned Source Cooperative parquet snapshots or the rfishbase R package. Public technical access is snapshot-based and may lag the live website.
